title: Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Bill
what_it_is: Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Bill

sections.label: Sea level rise projections
sections.summary: Singapore's Third National Climate Change Study projects sea levels may rise up to 1.15 metres by end of century, flooding around 30% of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Singapore's Third National Climate Change Study (V3) projects that our sea levels may rise up to 1.15 metres by the end of this century, reaching up to five metres above today's mean sea level when coupled with storm surges and high tides.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: It means that around 30% of Singapore could be flooded by seawater.

sections.label: Coastal Protection Bill introduction
sections.summary: The Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Bill introduces legislative and regulatory levers, adding coastal protection elements into the Sewerage and Drainage Act, renamed the Sewerage, Drainage and Coastal Protection Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The implementation needs to be carefully phased, to take into account the resources available and to tie in with other development timelines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We are thus introducing the Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Bill, or "the Bill" for short, principally to introduce legislative and regulatory levers to undergird coastal protection work moving forward.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: These new coastal protection elements will be introduced into the existing Sewerage and Drainage Act (SDA), which will be renamed the Sewerage, Drainage and Coastal Protection Act (SDCPA).

sections.label: Landowner coastal protection duty
sections.summary: Under new section 30E, each landowner must ensure a coastal protection measure for the Prescribed Place by a stipulated date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Under the new section 30E of the Bill, each landowner must ensure that there is a coastal protection measure for the Prescribed Place by a stipulated date.

sections.label: Government and Statutory Boards implementation
sections.summary: The majority of coastal protection measures will be implemented by the Government and Statutory Boards, which own about 70% of the coastline.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The majority of the coastal protection measures will be implemented by the Government and Statutory Boards as they own about 70% of the coastline.

sections.label: Grant coverage for coastal works
sections.summary: The grant will cover the cost of studies, services diversion, and construction necessary to implement coastal protection measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The grant will cover the cost of studies, services diversion, as well as the construction necessary to implement coastal protection measures.

sections.label: Connecting with adjacent neighbours
sections.summary: Section 30G requires landowners to connect their coastal protection measures with their adjacent neighbours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Section 30G requires landowners to connect their coastal protection measures with their adjacent neighbours.

sections.label: Flood response plans for landowners
sections.summary: Landowners in transiently floodable coastal areas must prepare a flood response plan and conduct periodic drills under section 30L.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: To ensure public safety in transiently floodable areas along the coast, where transient flooding might occur, landowners of premises within the areas will be required under section 30L to prepare a flood response plan and periodically conduct drills based on the flood response plan.

sections.label: Advance notice to Prescribed Places landowners
sections.summary: PUB will endeavour to inform landowners of Prescribed Places of their obligations about 10 years before the expected completion date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: To provide landowners of Prescribed Places with sufficient lead time to fulfil their obligations, PUB will endeavour to inform them of their obligations about 10 years ahead of the expected completion date.

sections.label: Five years to implement measures
sections.summary: Landowners will have at least five years from the Second Notification to implement their measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Landowners will have at least five years from the Second Notification to implement their measures.

sections.label: Commencement of SDA amendments
sections.summary: The SDA amendments commence this year, but landowners' legal obligations begin closer to the early 2030s after boundaries are gazetted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the SDA which I mentioned, will commence this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: That said, affected landowners’ legal obligations will only begin taking effect closer to early 2030s, after the Absolute Protection Boundaries and Protection Boundaries are gazetted.

sections.label: Singapore's sea level rise risk
sections.summary: Projected sea level rises of up to 1.15 metres by 2100 and two metres by 2150 affect Singapore, where over 30% of land is under five metres above sea level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: We were fortunate to be spared from this catastrophic calamity as well as other extreme climatic conditions such as typhoons and floods that often befall our closest neighbours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: But with projections of rising sea levels of up to 1.15 metres by 2100 and up to two metres by 2150, we must remember that more than 30% of Singapore's land area is less than five metres above sea level.

sections.label: Companies affected by Bill
sections.summary: Up to 100 companies are estimated to be affected by this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Up to 100 companies are estimated to be affected by this Bill.

sections.label: Coastal and Flood Protection Fund
sections.summary: The passage states $5 billion was topped up in 2025 to the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund and asks the Minister to consider a centralised approach to coastal protection design and construction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In terms of funding, $5 billion had been topped up in 2025 to the national Coastal and Flood Protection Fund (CFPF).

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Coastal protection is a candidate for the latter even if we want to harness the power of the former.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I ask the Minister to consider a centralised approach towards the design and construction of all coastal protection measures to ensure the most robust outcomes.

sections.label: Notice for coastal protection works
sections.summary: Authorities have clarified that owners will receive a minimum of 10 years' notice to carry out these works, with deadlines tailored to individual site studies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Authorities have clarified that owners will receive a minimum of 10 years' notice to carry out these works, with specific deadlines tailored to the findings and progress of individual site studies.

sections.label: Financial support grant framework timeline
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister can provide a definitive timeline for the announcement of the financial support grant framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide a definitive timeline for the announcement of the financial support grant framework?

sections.label: Lease extensions tied to coastal protection
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister will consider a framework where lease extensions are tied to coastal protection investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Further, will the Minister also consider a framework where lease extensions are tied to coastal protection investments?

sections.label: Annual coastal resilience report
sections.summary: The passage expresses hope that the Government will consider tabling an annual coastal resilience report detailing Coastal and Flood Protection Fund disbursements and progress across public and private sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For greater transparency on fund usage and decision-making, I hope the Government will consider tabling an annual coastal resilience report detailing Coastal and Flood Protection Fund disbursements and progress across both public and private sectors.

sections.label: Private lessees with short leases
sections.summary: The passage states the Government will provide financial and technical assistance to landowners but details are not yet announced, and asks whether many affected private lessees have remaining lease terms under 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I understand that the Government will provide financial and technical assistance to landowners, but the specific details have not yet been announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether there are many affected private lessees who currently have remaining lease terms of less than 10 years.

sections.label: Coastal defence project delay concerns
sections.summary: Speaker worries businesses may lack funds or go bankrupt, and suggests progress indicators or a performance bond to keep coastal defence works on schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While the 10-year timeline is long enough, I am concerned about how we can prevent project delays due to businesses having insufficient financial resources or going bandkrupt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I suggest that the authorities should establish progress indicators or consider implementing a performance bond system to ensure that coastal defence works can be completed on schedule.

sections.label: Kampung heritage in coastal defence
sections.summary: Speaker urges cultural heritage assessment in engineering so coastal defence works do not sacrifice kampung heritage or cultural landmarks, and supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Fourth, as we strengthen our coastal defences, we must never sacrifice kampung heritage or cultural landmarks for the sake of engineering efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I suggest incorporating cultural heritage assessment into the engineering process, so that while protecting our land, we can also safeguard the collective memory of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Although I have the above concerns, I support this Bill.

sections.label: PUB consultation with private coastal owners
sections.summary: Speaker asks how extensive PUB's consultations were with the roughly 30% of private owners or lessors of Singapore's coastal line.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: While PUB consulted a wide range of stakeholders for the purposes of our coastal protection plan, how extensive were its consultations with the roughly 30% of the private owners or lessors of our Singapore coastal line?

sections.label: Opt-in, updates, legal requisition
sections.summary: Speaker suggests an opt-in for private owners' Coastal Protection Measures, asks if progress updates to PUB are required, and asks how agencies ensure requirements appear at the legal requisition stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, perhaps PUB could consider an "opt-in", at least for the implementation or installation of the Costal Protection Measures for private owners or lessors instead of requiring them to procure the same from scratch.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Thirdly, in the 10-year period for private owners and lessors to plan and implement Coastal Protection Measures, will they be required to provide progress updates to PUB?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Lastly, speaking from the perspective of conveyancing lawyer, how does the agencies ensure that the requirements are accurately reflected during the legal requisition stage?

sections.label: Projected sea level rise
sections.summary: Singapore's climate scientists project sea levels could rise up to 1.15 metres by 2100 and two metres by the middle of the next century, submerging Kallang, Marine Parade and parts of the CBD.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's own climate scientists project sea levels around our island could rise by up to 1.15 metres by 2100, and up to two metres by the middle of the next century.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To put that in perspective, a two-metre rise would submerge most of Kallang and Marine Parade, and parts of the Central Business District as well.

sections.label: Mangroves dissipate wave energy
sections.summary: A 2025 study in Nature's Communication, Earth and Environment found mangrove forests wider than 500 metres dissipate at least 75% of incoming wave energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A 2025 study in Nature's Communication, Earth and Environment found that mangrove forests wider than 500 metres dissipate at least 75% of incoming wave energy.

sections.label: Singapore coastal protection funding
sections.summary: Singapore is committing $100 billion over 100 years to coastal protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore is committing $100 billion over 100 years to coastal protection.

sections.label: Global coastal flooding exposure study
sections.summary: A 2019 study found 300 million people will face annual coastal flooding by 2050, with Asian nations most exposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A landmark 2019 study in Nature Communications found that by 2050, land currently home to 300 million people will experience annual coastal flooding and five of the six most exposed nations are in Asia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Ho Chi Minh City already loses $1.3 billion annually to coastal flooding and the Maldives faces projected damages of up to 12.5% of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2100.

sections.label: Dutch water export sector
sections.summary: The Dutch water export sector generates nearly €10 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Dutch water export sector generates nearly €10 billion annually.

sections.label: Singapore tropical coastal resilience export strategy
sections.summary: An MP asks if a strategy exists to make Singapore a global centre for tropical coastal resilience and export expertise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The question is whether Singapore captures that value or whether we simply execute the work and let others package and export it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, I would ask the Minister if there is a deliberate strategy to position Singapore as the global centre of excellence for tropical coastal resilience to ensure that the expertise developed through this $100 billion programme generates not just a protected coastline for Singapore but a new export industry, one that creates high-value jobs for Singaporeans and allows us to serve Jakarta, Manila, Dhaka and the small island states of the Pacific with solutions designed for their conditions.

sections.label: Ayer Rajah coastal businesses obligations
sections.summary: Ayer Rajah's coastal areas include private businesses that must implement, operate and maintain coastal protection measures under new legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Ayer Rajah extends across southwest of Singapore's coast.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: It includes the coastal areas that are home to several private businesses that, under this new legislation, must implement, operate and maintain coastal protection measures.

sections.label: Advance notice for coastal protection
sections.summary: Landowners will be given at least 10 years' advance notice to implement coastal protection measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Landowners will be given at least 10 years' advance notice to implement coastal protection measures.

sections.label: Government support for affected businesses
sections.summary: The Government announced it will provide affected businesses with technical and financial support, with details disclosed later.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The Government has announced that it will provide businesses affected with both technical and financial support and I appreciate that details will be disclosed at the appropriate juncture.

sections.label: Upfront disbursements versus reimbursements
sections.summary: Upfront disbursements give business owners greater certainty and ease cash flow concerns, while reimbursements may cause more hesitation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Upfront disbursements would provide business owners with greater certainty and allay concerns around cash flow, while subsequent reimbursements may cause more hesitation amongst business owners.

sections.label: Financing coastal protection as investment
sections.summary: Financial instruments like sustainability-linked insurance or green bonds may let the private sector structure coastal protection financing as investment rather than cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Financial instruments, such as sustainability-linked insurance or green bonds, may allow the private sector to structure the financing for coastal protection measures as an investment rather than cost.

sections.label: State-managed coastline share
sections.summary: On technical support, 70% of Singapore's coastline is state-managed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: On technical support, 70% of Singapore's coastline is state-managed.

sections.label: Coral reef loss since 1960s
sections.summary: More than two-thirds of Singapore's coral reefs have been lost to coastal development and reclamation since the 1960s.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: More than two-thirds of Singapore's coral reefs have been lost to coastal development and reclamation since 1960s.

sections.label: Coastal Protection Bill support
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Bill and is committed to a continuous coastal protection line against climate change risk, with responsibility shared between Government and private parties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I support the Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Bill and is committed to establishing a continuous coastal protection line to effectively address the risk brought by climate change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This Bill makes coastal protection a responsibility shared between the Government and private parties.

sections.label: Clear rules and business risk
sections.summary: It states that lacking clear rules raises business risks in transactions or financing, making businesses more conservative and less willing to invest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: If clear rules are lacking, businesses will face higher risks during transaction or financing and may therefore become more conservative, affecting their overall investment willingness.

sections.label: List of professional consultants
sections.summary: It gives an example of integrating resources into a list of professional consultants and contractors for industry reference to cut costs and uncertainties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: For example, integrating resources to form a list of professional consultants and contractors for industry reference to reduce cost and uncertainties for businesses when selecting professional capabilities and improve overall project quality.

sections.label: Coral reefs and sea levels
sections.summary: It states Singapore lost about two-thirds of its coral reefs since the 1960s and urges stronger impact assessments and nature-based coastal protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Our country has lost about two-thirds of its coral reefs since the 1960s, while existing ones mainly distributed in the Southern waters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to strengthen environment impact assessments when implementing projects and adopt nature-based solutions to enhance coastal protection capabilities while protecting our marine ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By the year 2100, sea levels would have risen to 1.15 metres, possibly surging to five metres during weather events.

sections.label: Decentralised responsibility to landowners
sections.summary: It states implementation must be consistent and well-integrated, but the Bill decentralises responsibility to individual landowners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This means implementation must be consistent and well-integrated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, under this Bill, the responsibility is decentralised to individual landowners.

sections.label: Bill and business competitiveness
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government has assessed how the Bill will affect business competitiveness for coastal landowners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Has the Government assessed how this Bill will affect business competitiveness for our coastal landowners?

sections.label: Contingency plans for support
sections.summary: It asks whether contingency plans are in place to provide support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Do we have contingency plans in place to provide support?

sections.label: Coastal resilience need
sections.summary: Nearly 30% of Singapore lies under five metres above mean sea level, making stronger coastal resilience clearly necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: When close to 30% of our island lies less than five metres above mean sea level, the need to strengthen our coastal resilience is clear.

sections.label: Clause 13 landowner obligations
sections.summary: Clause 13 obligates landowners to maintain coastal protection measures meeting standards; a City-East Coast study began in 2021 costing $18 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Under clause 13 of the Bill, landowners are obligated to ensure that there is at all times a coastal protection measure for the prescribed place that meets the coastal protection measures standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It was reported that coastal protection site-specific study for the City-East Coast region, including areas, such as East Coast Park, began in 2021 and cost $18 million.

sections.label: Seamless connection between plots
sections.summary: Proposed section 30G requires landowners and long-term lessees of coastal land to connect their coastal protection measures seamlessly with adjacent plots.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Under the proposed new section 30G of the Sewerage and Drainage Act, landowners and long-term lessees of coastal land must ensure that their coastal protection measures connect seamlessly with those on adjacent plots.

sections.label: System-level coastal coordination
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry will ensure system-level coordination so coastal defence is coherent rather than fragmented, requiring a system-wide approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Left purely to neighbouring parties, coordination may become complex.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: More broadly, coastal protection along an industrial coastline often involves inter-dependencies across multiple sites, not just between two neighbouring plots.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry ensure that coordination occurs at the system level, so that the resulting infrastructure forms a coherent and effective defence rather than a series of fragmented measures?

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Much like our water systems, power grids and transport networks, protecting Singapore's coastline ultimately requires a coordinated, system-wide approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The resilience of our coast should not depend on isolated pockets of protection, but on a continuous and well-planned defence of the entire shoreline.

sections.label: PUB guidance for landowners
sections.summary: The passage asks how PUB will guide and support landowners toward holistic, long-term coastal protection rather than lowest-cost or short-term retrofits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share how PUB will guide and support landowners to take a holistic and long-term approach to coastal protection, rather than prioritising lowest-cost or short-term retrofits?

sections.label: Continuity after ownership change
sections.summary: The passage asks how planning continuity and coordination with new owners will be ensured if coastal land changes ownership after requirements or boundaries are designated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Bill allows for up to 10 years for owners to implement measures, which is helpful for long-term planning and coordination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry clarify how continuity of planning and coordination with new owners will be ensured if and when coastal land changes ownership after the protection requirements or boundaries have been designated?

sections.label: Financial and technical support request
sections.summary: A request for the Ministry to outline financial and technical support available over the years for landowners during implementation and maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As investment costs may be significant, it would be helpful if the Ministry could outline a little bit more, the financial and technical support available over the years, so as to provide greater assurance to landowners during implementation and more importantly for maintenance in the years to come as such measures will need to remain robust and effective?

sections.label: Landowners responsible for coastal protection
sections.summary: Landowners should be responsible for coastal protection measures on their land.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Fundamentally, landowners should be responsible for the coastal protection measures on their land.

sections.label: No cost recovery from landowners
sections.summary: The Government will not recover costs of centralised coastal protection schemes from protected landowners, and will own, implement and operate the coastal barriers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Ms Nadia Samdin asked if we would charge landowners who will be protected by centralised coastal protection schemes, such as the coastal barriers at the Greater Southern Waterfront.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We will not be recovering the cost of these measures from the landowners, just like how we are not imposing any costs on inland landowners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: These costs will be borne by the Government, who will own, implement and operate the coastal barriers.

sections.label: Lessor or lessee obligations
sections.summary: Under new section 2D, the Government will make clear in regulations whether the lessor or lessee is considered for coastal protection obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Under the new section 2D of the Bill, the Government will make clear in regulations whether the lessor or the lessee is considered for the relevant coastal protection obligations.

sections.label: Coastal Protection Code of Practice
sections.summary: PUB aims to publish the Coastal Protection Code of Practice later this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: PUB aims to publish the Coastal Protection Code of Practice, as I mentioned earlier in the speech.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: This Code of Practice will be published later this year.

sections.label: PUB maintenance and forced entry powers
sections.summary: PUB has powers to undertake maintenance and repair works and recover costs from landowners, and powers of forced entry during imminent coastal floods when landowners are unresponsive or uncontactable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: First, PUB has power under sections 41 and 44 to step in and undertake maintenance and repair works to ensure the functionality of the continuous line of defence and to recover the cost as necessary from the landowner subsequently.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Second, PUB has powers of forced entry, which we will use in the scenario when there is an imminent coastal flood, but the landowner does not have a fully implemented coastal protection measure in place and is unresponsive or uncontactable, notwithstanding efforts to contact them.

sections.label: Grant tracking and landowner reimbursement
sections.summary: The grant's tracking and landownership changes are being considered, with reimbursement to the landowner in tranches.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Ms Lee Hui Ying also asked how the grant will be tracked and how it will account for changes in landownership.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We are considering reimbursing the landowner in tranches.

sections.label: Environmental impact assessments for coastal works
sections.summary: Coastal protection works in sensitive areas or with transboundary impact need consultation, and significant impact requires an environmental study and mitigation measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Ms Cassandra Lee also asked whether environmental impact assessments will be required.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We would like to assure the Member that coastal protection works in or near sensitive areas or that have potential transboundary impact will need to undergo in-depth consultation with technical agencies on the site's potential ecological and biodiversity value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: If there is potentially significant environmental impact, agencies will require an environmental study to assess the full impact of the works and develop more extensive mitigation measures.

sections.label: PUB gazetting protection boundaries
sections.summary: As a regulatory authority, PUB will gazette the scope of Absolute Protection Boundaries and Protection Boundaries to demarcate Prescribed Places.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As a regulatory authority, PUB will gazette the scope of the "Absolute Protection Boundaries" and "Protection Boundaries" to demarcate Prescribed Places.

sections.label: PUB technical advice and grants
sections.summary: PUB will provide technical advice and grants to assist in fulfilling coastal protection obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: PUB will also provide technical advice and grants to assist them in fulfilling their coastal protection obligations.

sections.label: Bill foundation for coastal defence
sections.summary: The Bill lays the foundation for a continuous line of defence protecting Singapore against sea level rise for 50, 100 years and more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In fact, as Mr Andre Low has alluded to and explained so passionately, there could be new opportunities generated for us as we build up expertise and experience in coastal protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: This Bill lays the foundation to ensure a continuous line of defence that will protect Singapore against sea level rise for the next 50, 100 years and more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Together, we will work together for a more resilient and prosperous Singapore amidst the rising seas.

sections.label: Responsibility lies with landowner
sections.summary: Responsibility will have to lie with the landowner that has executed the work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The first question on responsibility, it will have to lie with the landowner that has executed the work.

sections.label: Connection responsibility for later joiner
sections.summary: A party joining an already built structure must ensure the connection is water-tight.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: If you are the later one that is joining to one that is already been built, it is your responsibility to ensure that there is connection and that the connection is water-tight.

sections.label: Coastal protection checks and entry procedures
sections.summary: Coastal protection measures are checked, and if landowners cannot be contacted, PUB follows standard operating procedures and may enter premises with senior management approval.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: They can check, make sure that all the coastal protection measures are in place and working as they are intended to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: But if we are really unable to contact them, we will have some standard operating procedures – x number of hours from the expected time of arrival of the weather event, PUB will then have to execute.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And if they are unable to contact the landowner by a certain time and they have to access, they have no alternative except to enter the premises to erect some of these measures, then they have to seek the approval from their senior management and they will have enough time to erect temporary measures and interim measures.

sections.label: Tidal gates at Sentosa and Keppel Bay
sections.summary: Tidal gates are built at coastal areas in Sentosa and Keppel Bay where possible to keep the coastline pleasant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: You have seen the design reflecting the collective thinking on what is optimal for the country.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, where it is possible, we build tidal gates at the coastal area in Sentosa, in Keppel Bay, so that we can keep the coastline as pleasant as it is now.

sections.label: Absolute Protection Boundary trade-offs
sections.summary: The Absolute Protection Boundary is set after considering where to minimise environmental impact while maximising protection of properties and lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: If Singapore is flooded, it is difficult for us to protect other things around us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, we also need to have some boundary, and so the Absolute Protection Boundary is set after due consideration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Where would be the appropriate line to be drawn so that we minimise the impact on the environment, so we maximise the protection of properties and lives – because that is the trade off that we are balancing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We want to be friendly to the environment, but at the same time we have to ensure that that is still an absolute boundary that is absolutely critical, crucial for the protection of our properties, our homes, our cars, our businesses and our lives.
